from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 7  # sources
    J = 9  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [202, 129, 117, 174, 130, 108, 179]
    demands = [59, 43, 47, 43, 47, 34, 37, 40, 37]
    cost_matrix = [[5.51, 20.18, 17.03, 13.03, 21.83, 27.19, 12.35, 15.03, 23.78], [8.27, 28.07, 15.1, 22.74, 15.19, 21.72, 13.65, 27.16, 4.29], [3.68, 19.02, 17.79, 4.6, 22.05, 22.41, 24.42, 19.44, 5.71], [20.48, 29.93, 7.44, 24.83, 7.79, 23.22, 16.3, 7.25, 3.83], [15.24, 29.41, 21.76, 14.92, 7.93, 28.36, 3.29, 13.32, 7.35], [20.36, 17.23, 19.25, 10.6, 16.65, 21.64, 22.85, 14.04, 12.89], [15.23, 8.01, 29.77, 3.36, 12.94, 23.07, 28.75, 28.78, 24.34]]
    emission_matrix = [[8.37, 8.11, 12.33, 16.37, 10.16, 9.26, 6.52, 3.53, 12.96], [18.95, 5.78, 12.46, 9.89, 16.19, 6.52, 12.87, 13.9, 16.31], [8.65, 7.53, 12.97, 6.09, 7.26, 12.84, 2.68, 11.41, 16.1], [7.8, 12.94, 18.7, 12.52, 6.79, 3.51, 8.24, 15.94, 17.27], [15.91, 1.0, 11.18, 10.96, 10.41, 5.7, 6.15, 6.46, 20.0], [15.42, 14.94, 10.86, 9.11, 10.9, 17.4, 4.83, 4.84, 9.12], [16.23, 7.81, 1.77, 19.96, 10.55, 14.2, 1.79, 10.3, 12.12]]
    fixed_costs = [[250, 133, 252, 258, 73, 177, 281, 243, 69], [210, 153, 99, 276, 186, 67, 138, 211, 261], [181, 159, 258, 156, 219, 228, 268, 109, 121], [223, 112, 136, 207, 206, 68, 190, 152, 89], [128, 61, 277, 155, 182, 63, 150, 194, 125], [81, 277, 217, 202, 264, 211, 281, 104, 134], [75, 185, 179, 181, 70, 201, 71, 273, 133]]
    moq = [[15, 7, 9, 11, 8, 6, 15, 20, 19], [13, 5, 14, 16, 11, 19, 13, 17, 7], [10, 6, 14, 15, 20, 6, 20, 7, 19], [8, 19, 9, 8, 8, 8, 7, 16, 11], [5, 11, 14, 8, 19, 20, 16, 14, 16], [17, 13, 20, 8, 10, 18, 9, 15, 13], [12, 9, 7, 6, 6, 19, 9, 18, 8]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Executive Supply Chain Leadership
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Date: Today
Subject: Balancing Cost and Carbon in Route Activation and Shipments

Context
Our distribution network moves product from multiple warehouses to multiple stores. Each possible route between a warehouse and a store carries two meaningful per‑unit measures: a monetary shipping cost and a CO2 emission rate. In many cases, the lowest‑cost lanes also have higher carbon intensity, so an explicit balance is necessary to protect margin while advancing our sustainability commitments.

Operational Rules We Must Respect
- Route activation fees: Using any lane requires a one‑time setup charge that covers contracting, compliance, and dock readiness. A route is either active or not; once active, the fee applies in full regardless of volume shipped on that lane.
- Minimum order quantities: Activated routes must move at least a specified floor of units to justify equipment and handling. Partial loads below this threshold are not accepted.
- Supplier limits per store: To manage receiving capacity, vendor oversight, and contract simplicity, each store may be served by no more than a fixed number of warehouses within the plan period.

Management Priority
Leadership has directed that cost efficiency carries more weight than emissions reduction, while still keeping emissions materially in scope. In practice, we will evaluate route choices using a blended measure that combines variable shipping spend and total emissions according to the set weights. Importantly, route activation fees are added to the plan at their full value and are not part of the weighting between cost and emissions.

Planning Guardrails
- Warehouse supply limits: Total outbound volume from each warehouse will not exceed available inventory or allocation for the planning window.
- Store demand requirements: Each store’s demand must be met in full at or above the stated minimum requirement.
- Activation and minimums: Any lane we turn on will ship at least its minimum order quantity.
- Supplier caps: No store will receive from more than the allowed number of warehouses.

Goal and Deliverable
Our aim is to identify which routes to activate and how much to ship on each active lane so that:
- We meet all store demand without exceeding warehouse availability.
- We respect the minimum‑order and supplier‑cap rules to keep operations practical and compliant.
- We reduce the blended measure of total variable cost and total emissions according to management’s weights, while including all route setup fees in full.

The deliverable will be a recommended activation list and shipment plan by lane, accompanied by summaries of projected spend and emissions. We will also highlight where the plan chooses a higher‑cost, lower‑emission route versus a lower‑cost, higher‑emission route so leadership can see the trade‑offs implied by the current weights. If priorities shift, we can update the weights and re‑run the evaluation to reflect new guidance.
